title: Instagram Feed Design
description: Study how Instagram designs its feed service for photo-heavy content, including storage, CDN, recommendation algorithms, and real-time ranking.

data.text: Instagram's feed is a photo and video stream served to over 2 billion users. Unlike Twitter's text-heavy timeline, Instagram's feed is dominated by large media files, real-time ranking, and aggressive caching to minimize load times on mobile networks.

Instagram uses a pre-computed feed model. When a user scrolls, the app requests the next page of posts from a feed service. The service queries a ranked list of post IDs from a cache and fetches media URLs from a CDN. Ranking happens asynchronously via a batch job.

data.text: Instagram stores photos and videos in object storage (Amazon S3 or equivalent) and serves them through a globally distributed CDN. Each post generates multiple resolutions: thumbnail (150x150), low (320x320), medium (640x640), and high (1080x1080). The CDN caches these at edge locations near users.

data.title: CDN Caching Strategy
data.text: Instagram's CDN serves over 80% of media requests from cache. Images are cached for days; videos are cached for hours. Cache invalidation uses versioned URLs so new uploads are immediately available.

Feed ranking uses a machine learning model that predicts engagement (likes, comments, shares, saves) for each post-user pair. The model considers post age, user interaction history, relationship strength, and content type. The top 100 posts by predicted score are returned.

data.title: Instagram Feed Lessons
points: Pre-computed feeds with async ranking balance freshness and latency
CDN is mandatory for media-heavy applications
Multiple resolutions serve different device and network conditions
ML ranking replaces chronological feeds in modern social apps
data.takeaway: Instagram's feed proves that great UX requires pre-computation, ML ranking, and global CDN — not just raw infrastructure.

data.title: Estimate Instagram Feed Capacity
data.description: Instagram has 2 billion users, each viewing 50 posts per session with 10 sessions per day. At 200 KB average per post, estimate daily bandwidth and monthly storage with 3x replication.
data.expectedOutcome: Daily bandwidth = 2B x 50 x 10 x 200KB = 200 PB; daily storage = 2B x 500 x 200KB = 200 PB; monthly with 3x replication = 1800 PB
